best_facts.fact: Nepal's interim Prime Minister in September 2025, former Chief Justice Sushila Karki, was picked with the help of an online poll that protesters ran on a Discord chat server.
best_facts.why_surprising: A head of government partly chosen on a gaming chat app.

best_facts.fact: Ceaușescu went from being booed on live television on 21 December 1989 to being executed on 25 December: four days from a crowd's whistles to the end of 24 years of rule.
best_facts.why_surprising: Absolute power evaporated within a week.

best_facts.fact: The Berlin Wall opened because a spokesman misread a note at a press conference and said the new travel rules applied immediately, without delay.
best_facts.why_surprising: A 28-year wall fell to a briefing error.

best_facts.fact: Archaeologists found 190 ostraka bearing Themistocles' name written by only about 14 hands, suggesting ballots were mass-produced and handed out to voters in ancient Athens.
best_facts.why_surprising: Pre-printed ballots and party workers are 2,400 years old.

best_facts.fact: Ju/'hoansi hunters in the Kalahari deliberately insult a successful hunter's kill as skinny and worthless so that he never starts thinking of himself as a chief.
best_facts.why_surprising: Equality is enforced by mockery.

best_facts.fact: In Milgram's best-known version, 26 of 40 ordinary volunteers kept pressing switches up to the maximum 450 volts because a man in a lab coat told them to continue.
best_facts.why_surprising: Two-thirds obeyed a stranger's authority to apparent cruelty.

best_facts.fact: Women in the Swiss canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden got the vote on cantonal matters only in 1990, when the federal court forced it, and men there traditionally showed a sword as proof of citizenship.
best_facts.why_surprising: A model direct democracy excluded women until 1990.

best_facts.fact: The giant on the cover of Hobbes's Leviathan is made of more than 300 tiny people, all facing the king's head.
best_facts.why_surprising: The state is drawn literally as the people combined.

best_facts.fact: Machiavelli never wrote 'the ends justify the means'; the nearest line in The Prince says only that people judge princes by the outcome.
best_facts.why_surprising: The most famous Machiavelli quote is not his.

best_facts.fact: Rousseau wrote the 'let them eat cake' story around 1765, when Marie Antoinette was about nine years old and living in Austria.
best_facts.why_surprising: The cake line predates her arrival in France.

best_facts.fact: The Nazi party never won a majority in a free national election; its best result was 37.3% in July 1932, and Hitler was appointed Chancellor by elites who thought they could control him.
best_facts.why_surprising: The most famous 'elected dictator' was appointed, not elected by a majority.

best_facts.fact: Sri Lanka's President Gotabaya Rajapaksa fled after protesters swam in his official pool in July 2022, and he resigned by email from Singapore.
best_facts.why_surprising: A presidency ended in an inbox.

best_facts.fact: All of India's indelible election ink has come from one public company in Mysuru, Mysore Paints and Varnish, since 1962; the firm was founded by a Maharaja in 1937.
best_facts.why_surprising: A royal varnish factory supplies the proof of democracy.

best_facts.fact: Ashoka's own 13th rock edict records that 100,000 people were killed in his conquest of Kalinga, and that he felt remorse.
best_facts.why_surprising: An emperor published his own body count and regret.

best_facts.fact: Magna Carta failed as a peace deal: the Pope annulled it about ten weeks after King John sealed it in 1215.
best_facts.why_surprising: The world's most famous charter of liberty was void within months.

best_facts.fact: Nonviolent campaigns against regimes and occupations from 1900 to 2006 succeeded about 53% of the time, twice the 26% rate of violent ones.
best_facts.why_surprising: Refusing is more effective than fighting.

best_facts.fact: India's Constitution was handwritten by a calligrapher, Prem Behari Narain Raizada, who charged no fee but asked for his name on every page.
best_facts.why_surprising: The founding law is a hand-lettered artwork.

best_facts.fact: Indira Gandhi lost her own seat in 1977 to Raj Narain, the man whose court case had voided her 1971 win and triggered the Emergency.
best_facts.why_surprising: The same rival beat her in court and then at the ballot box.

best_facts.fact: Bismarck created the world's first national health insurance in 1883 largely to undercut the socialists.
best_facts.why_surprising: The welfare state began as a tactic to buy loyalty.

best_facts.fact: V-Dem estimates that 74% of the world's people lived in autocracies in 2025, up from 50% in 2005.
best_facts.why_surprising: Most humans live in autocracies despite holding elections.

side_dish.title: Chimpanzee politics
side_dish.body_md:
In 1975 a young Dutch zoologist, **Frans de Waal**, began watching the chimpanzee colony at **Burgers Zoo** in Arnhem, the largest captive group in the world at the time. What he saw read like a court chronicle. An ageing alpha, Yeroen, lost his place to a younger rival, Luit. But Luit could not hold it alone. Yeroen threw his support to a third male, Nikkie, and the two of them ruled as a coalition, with Yeroen as the kingmaker taking a share of the mating privileges.

Power among chimps, de Waal found, was not just muscle. Alphas who lasted were the ones who built alliances, groomed supporters, broke up fights impartially and shared food. Females, led by an old matriarch called Mama, could block a male who had not won the group's acceptance. That is something very like legitimacy: rank that others are willing to accept.

De Waal published *Chimpanzee Politics* in 1982. The US House Speaker **Newt Gingrich** later put it on a reading list for new Republican members of Congress. Later work showed that bullying alphas tend to be overthrown, sometimes violently, while those who act as peacekeepers keep power longer.

The lesson for today's topic: Machiavelli's question, love or fear, is older than our species. Even among apes, power that relies on force alone is expensive and brittle. De Waal died in March 2024.

offline_task.title: Map the authority in one ordinary day
offline_task.body_md:
Today, notice every time someone gets you to do something, or you get someone else to.

1. Keep a short list: the traffic signal, a manager's message, a parent's request, a building guard, an app's notification, a queue.
2. For each, write which it was: **power** (you had no real choice), **authority** (you obeyed because you accept their right to ask), or **persuasion** (you agreed on the merits).
3. For each authority, write which of Weber's types it was: tradition, charisma or rules.
4. Pick one where you obeyed without thinking. Ask: what would happen if I and ten others refused? That is the question every regime fears.
5. At night, read one news story and ask the three questions: who can make whom do what, do the people obeying think it is rightful, and what would make them stop?

Keep the list. You will notice that almost nothing in your day ran on force alone.
